correctness.rationale: The two signed descent/ascent steps act respectively by I−rS and I+rS, with noise signs −h,+h. Thus the pair endpoint is a z+h[ξ₁−(I+rS)ξ₀], with a=1−r². Centering and independent pairs give the exact sum of innovation second moments, with geometric ratio a²; the horizon and invariant-risk optima reduce to the same positive multiple of the one-pair cost. In the two swap eigendirections the marginal variances are v and Cauchy–Schwarz gives cost at least v(|1±r|−1)² per coordinate. Nonzero multipliers force equality or sign reversal almost surely; isotropy makes both equalities feasible together. At r=1 the plus equality remains necessary, and one can take an independent minus output with the prescribed marginal. Consequently the optimizer is unique off r=1 among arbitrary joint laws, as claimed. Division by 1−a²=r²(2−r²) gives the stationary formulas; independent noise has total pair cost v(4+2r²), and identical reuse has 2vr². The finite-horizon and small-r limits follow. The conditional-unbiasedness caveat concerns conditioning on the full information after the first call; with that requirement the cross term is zero. Bounded exact reproduction checked multipliers and several horizons, including R*=18/41 at r=3/5 and swap/reuse/independent risks 26/7,36/7,86/7 at r=6/5 with σ=v=1.
residual_risks: Only the scalar, fixed-marginal, pair-independent Gaussian oracle and stable range are claimed. The second call can be conditionally biased after the first call.
